brief.outcome: Get the cost of each booked plumbing job from Google Ads under 90 dollars within three months, while booked jobs per month stay at least as high as today and the Austin service area stays the same.
brief.deliverable: A tracked, cleaned-up Google Ads account where leads can be tied to booked jobs in Housecall Pro, with approved changes applied and a monthly read of cost per booked job in the owner's Google Sheet.
done: The real cost per booked job and the real number of booked jobs a month are measured, not guessed
Calls, forms and booked jobs can be tied back to Google Ads, or the limits are stated
Wasted spend is found by search term, hour and campaign, and the owner has chosen what to change
Approved changes are applied one at a time with registered tests
Cost per booked job and booked jobs are read against the 90 dollar target and the no-drop guardrail
What was learned is saved for the next round

answers.question: What business and where?
answers.answer: Plumbing company with six vans in Austin, Texas.

answers.question: Spend and results now?
answers.answer: Google Ads spend is 6,000 dollars a month and we get about 120 leads, 50 dollars each (Google Ads dashboard).

answers.question: How many leads become jobs?
answers.answer: I think only a third become booked jobs but we do not track that properly.

answers.question: How are calls and bookings handled?
answers.answer: Calls go to a shared phone; we use Housecall Pro for bookings.

answers.answer: Google Ads MCP connected with live access, Housecall Pro exports only.

answers.question: What does success look like?
answers.answer: Cost per booked job under 90 dollars within three months, keeping booked jobs at least as high as now.

answers.answer: No changes to our service area. Keep data in a Google Sheet. I decide.

research.approach: Practitioners judge plumbing ads by cost per booked job, not cost per lead, so they fix measurement before touching bids. They confirm that calls and forms are counted once, tie ad clicks and calls to jobs that were really booked, then read the search terms report to cut DIY, job-seeker and parts searches, split campaigns by intent (emergency versus scheduled), tighten timing and location bids inside the area they serve, and send clicks to a service page with click-to-call. Automated bidding on a target cost is used only once there are enough tracked conversions, and each change is made one at a time and read over weeks so the account does not keep restarting its learning.

steps.name: Work out the real cost per booked job
steps.why: The 50 dollars per lead is a platform figure. Experts line up ad spend, calls and the jobs actually booked in the same dates to get cost per booked job and the number of booked jobs, which is also the guardrail.

steps.name: Fix call and form tracking and send booked jobs back to Google
steps.why: Calls and forms must each be counted once, short or junk calls filtered, and click IDs or call data kept so that booked jobs can be sent back. Bidding learns from what is counted, so counting booked jobs lets it chase jobs, not calls.

steps.name: Check that ad calls are answered and turn into bookings
steps.why: With one shared phone, missed or unanswered calls waste paid clicks. Experts compare calls from ads with calls answered and jobs created, by hour, before blaming the ads.

steps.name: Cut wasted searches with the search terms report
steps.why: The fastest saving is to stop paying for DIY, job-seeker and parts searches, tighten match types and add specific negatives, while avoiding negatives so broad they block real jobs.

steps.name: Split by intent and tighten timing and location inside the service area
steps.why: Emergency and scheduled work convert and cost differently. Experts separate them, adjust bids by hour and by zip code inside the area the business serves, and lower rather than switch off bids at quiet hours for round-the-clock services.

steps.name: Send clicks to a service page built to call or book
steps.why: Cost per lead is cost per click divided by conversion rate, so a page per service with click-to-call, trust signals, a stated service area and fast mobile loading lowers cost without touching bids.

steps.name: Choose bidding only after tracking is trusted
steps.why: Target-cost bidding needs enough tracked conversions and a learning period. Setting a target far below the current cost starves traffic, so experts verify tracking first and change one thing at a time.

steps.name: Run changes as one-at-a-time tests and read them against booked jobs
steps.why: Each change runs for weeks, with the booked-job guardrail checked, so improvements are real and the account does not keep restarting learning.

pitfalls.text: Judging by cost per lead or by calls, so cheap low-intent calls look like wins.
Counting a call and a form from the same visit twice, or counting very short calls as leads.
Adding broad negatives that block real jobs, or never refreshing the negative list.
Setting a bidding target far below current cost, or letting automated bidding run unsupervised.
Editing many things at once so no test can be read.

hypotheses.statement: The 50 dollars per lead is misleading because calls and forms are double counted or very short calls count as leads.
hypotheses.test: List the conversion actions and call length rules; compare Google Ads conversions with calls from ads and with Housecall Pro jobs created in the same dates.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Conversions exceed distinct calls and forms, or many counted calls are very short or unanswered.
hypotheses.refute_if: Conversions match distinct calls and forms and short calls are excluded.

hypotheses.statement: Many leads are not real jobs: wrong service, price shoppers, DIY questions or job seekers.
hypotheses.test: Join search terms and call outcomes to booked jobs; group non-booked leads by reason where recorded.
hypotheses.confirm_if: A large share of spend and leads sit on terms or call types that never book.
hypotheses.refute_if: Non-booked leads are mostly valid jobs lost after the call.

hypotheses.statement: Many ad calls to the shared phone go unanswered or are not followed up, so paid leads are lost.
hypotheses.test: Compare calls from ads with calls answered and jobs created within a day, by hour and weekday.
hypotheses.confirm_if: A meaningful share of ad calls is missed, concentrated at certain hours.
hypotheses.refute_if: Nearly all ad calls are answered and still do not book.

hypotheses.statement: Broad or phrase matching and thin negatives send spend to DIY, job-seeker and parts searches.
hypotheses.test: Search terms by spend and by booked jobs; share of spend on terms with clicks and no booked job.
hypotheses.confirm_if: A large share of spend goes to irrelevant terms with no booked jobs.
hypotheses.refute_if: Spend sits on relevant terms and most waste is small.

hypotheses.statement: Some hours, days or zip codes inside the service area waste spend.
hypotheses.test: Cost per booked job by hour, weekday and zip code inside the service area, with volume noted.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Segments with enough volume run far above average cost per booked job.
hypotheses.refute_if: Cost per booked job is flat across segments, or segments are too small to judge.

hypotheses.statement: Automated bidding optimises for cheap, low-intent calls because booked jobs are not counted.
hypotheses.test: Read bidding strategy, learning status and the conversions it optimises; compare cost per booked job by campaign.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Campaigns optimise for calls or forms and the cheapest sources have the worst booking rates.
hypotheses.refute_if: Booking rates are similar across campaigns, or bidding already uses booked-job data.

hypotheses.statement: Landing pages are slow or do not match the service searched, so clicks do not call.
hypotheses.test: Mobile speed, clicks to call and ad-to-page match for the top-spend ad groups; calls per click before and after any page change.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Slow pages, no click-to-call or a mismatch on high-spend ad groups.
hypotheses.refute_if: Pages are fast and match, and calls per click are healthy.

measurement.window: Read monthly across the three months; each test runs 2 to 4 weeks, and the account is not changed more than once per test.
measurement.min_volume: A verdict on a test needs the number of booked jobs the owner and AI agree before launch; below that the result is INCONCLUSIVE.
measurement.stop_rule: Revert a change if booked jobs fall below the baseline guardrail; otherwise run the full test window.
